lessons.title: Where your data goes
lessons.subtitle: Six review fields for every tool

sections.title: Check product and operation together
sections.content:
Where a prompt goes depends on product edition, contract, configuration and workflow. Check at least these six fields:

| Review field | Questions |
|---|---|
| **Roles** | Who is the controller, processor or another recipient? Is a processing agreement required and in place? |
| **Data flows** | Which content, metadata and logs leave which system, and in which regions are they stored or processed? |
| **Provider use** | Does the provider use inputs or outputs for model development, quality review or abuse monitoring? Which settings and commitments apply? |
| **Access and functions** | Which roles, permissions, connectors, extensions and sharing links are active? |
| **Lifecycle** | How long are inputs, outputs, logs and backups retained? How do access, deletion and export work? |
| **Organizational approval** | Which purposes, data classes, user groups and configurations does the approval cover? |

Cloud or local, free or paid, consumer or enterprise are sales categories. A local system can send telemetry and reach the network, and an enterprise contract does not cover every function and data class. Check the documents at procurement and after every material change.

sections.title: Shadow AI, and what works against it
sections.content:
Shadow AI is AI use for work that nobody approved. The classic case is a private chat account; extensions, new features in old software, personal API keys and local models outside the process count too.

It can lack contract, legal basis, permissions, data region, retention, logging and technical controls, and a "training off" switch settles none of this.

Counter it with a current approval matrix, clear data rules, reachable contacts, a checkable procurement path, usable approved alternatives and, by risk, access control, configuration policies, logging or blocking.

Before work use, check the published approval status for purpose, data class, product edition and active configuration.

quiz.questionText: Which option is safest for company data?

answerOptions.text: Any free service, because wide adoption counts as approval
An enterprise product approved by IT and data protection, in the reviewed configuration
A service with a European head office, unchecked product and data flows
There is no difference between the tools

quiz.explanation: Safe is what was checked: product, contract, permissions, data classes, tenant and data region. A brand name or a European head office checks none of it.

answerOptions.text: A particularly secure AI that runs in the background
AI tools the IT department uses itself
AI use for work that nobody approved
A privacy feature of a particular chat product

quiz.explanation: Any AI use for work without approval counts, including an extension or a personal API key. Who uses it, or how safe it looks, does not change that.

lessons.title: The four levels of data classification
lessons.subtitle: Which data belongs in which tool

sections.title: An example model with four levels
sections.content:
Your organization sets which data may go into which system. The four levels here are an example and map to no product names.

**Level 1, public:** What is already published, such as approved website copy and the product catalogue. You still check copyright, licences, embedded personal data, integrity and the tool approval.

**Level 2, internal:** What is not meant to leave the organization, such as project plans and meeting records. It belongs only in a workflow approved for this purpose and data class.

**Level 3, confidential:** What needs more protection in business, contractual or data protection terms, such as unpublished figures, customer lists and supplier terms. You need an approval plus reviewed contracts, configuration, permissions and retention, and depending on the case a legal basis or data protection impact assessment.

**Level 4, restricted:** What can do serious damage when lost or mishandled, such as health and payroll data, application documents and inventions before filing. General assistants are blocked by default; processing happens only in an expressly approved, tightly scoped system and workflow.

Passwords, API keys and other credentials belong in no prompt at any level.

sections.title: The decision tree
sections.content:
Before every input you answer five questions:

1. **Purpose:** What task should the system perform?
2. **Data and rights:** Which data types, people, copyrights, trade secrets or contractual duties are involved?
3. **Internal classification:** Which data class does your organization's policy assign?
4. **Approval:** Are product, configuration, extensions and workflow approved for exactly this use?
5. **Minimization:** What can you omit, anonymize or replace with a synthetic example?

If one answer is missing, you enter nothing and take the published approval or escalation route. A paid licence, an enterprise tenant and a disabled training setting answer none of the questions on their own. Cautious classification lowers the risk and replaces no legal basis, purpose limitation, authorization or contract.

quiz.questionText: An employee wants to process a customer list with names and email addresses in an unapproved AI service. Which statement holds?

answerOptions.text: Business contact details are always public and usable without further checks
A paid licence is approval enough
No processing until purpose, legal basis, data class and tool approval are settled
Digitally stored data may not be processed by software

quiz.explanation: Names and email addresses can be personal data. Purpose, legal basis, classification, contract, configuration and minimization, among other things, decide whether processing is permitted.

quiz.questionText: What do you do when a data item's confidentiality level is unclear?

answerOptions.text: Pick the lowest level so work does not stall
Stop the input and use the policy or the responsible approval function
Enter the data anyway and ask IT afterwards
Stop using AI tools entirely

quiz.explanation: Cautious classification is no approval. If the data class or the permitted workflow is unclear, settle it first and enter data afterwards.

sections.title: The exercise
sections.content:
The levels below are assumptions for a fictional company; your own policy applies to you.

| No. | Data item | Example level | Additional check |
|-----|-----------|---------------|------------------|
| 1 | Approved website copy | Public | Usage rights, personal data, currency |
| 2 | Internal meeting record | Internal | Participants, topics, consent or legal basis, approved workflow |
| 3 | Quarterly revenue before publication | Confidential | Market-disclosure, secrecy and access rules |
| 4 | Customer list with contact details | Confidential | Purpose, legal basis, processor terms, minimization |
| 5 | Payroll record | Restricted | Expressly approved specialist systems only, no general assistants |
| 6 | Published product catalogue | Public | Rights, version, approved use |
| 7 | Application documents | Restricted | Purpose limitation, access, retention, effects on applicants |
| 8 | Invention description before filing | Restricted | Patent and trade-secret controls, express approval required |
| 9 | Draft press release | Internal or confidential | Content and planned publication date |
| 10 | Supplier terms | Confidential | Contractual secrecy and permissions |

Note purpose, minimization, required approval and owner beside every row.

sections.title: What the table shows
sections.content:
- **Public (items 1 and 6):** You still check rights, personal data, currency and the tool rules.
- **Internal (item 2, sometimes item 9):** Stays inside the intended audience, only in the approved workflow and without details the purpose does not need.
- **Confidential (items 3, 4 and 10; item 9 depending on content):** Contract, legal basis, permissions, data region, retention and configuration have to fit the purpose, even for an enterprise product.
- **Restricted (items 5, 7 and 8):** General assistants are blocked. An exception needs a documented workflow reviewed on the technical and legal side.

A real policy also needs owners, approved products and functions, prohibited data, a reporting route for incidents and a process for new use cases.

quiz.questionText: How is an invention description before a patent filing handled under the example model?

answerOptions.text: As public, because it is a technical document
As internal; an enterprise subscription is enough for processing
As confidential; every local installation is automatically permitted
As restricted; only in an expressly approved workflow

quiz.explanation: Uncontrolled disclosure can cost novelty or trade-secret protection. The approved patent, security and data protection process decides whether processing is permitted, in the cloud or locally.

quiz.questionText: An internal meeting record is to be summarized with AI. Which selection rule holds?

answerOptions.text: Any service is suitable if the record contains no figures
Only a workflow approved for it, with unnecessary details removed
No system is ever suitable, not even an approved one
Every local installation is automatically suitable

quiz.explanation: A record can carry personal, confidential or restricted content. Product, contract, recording and transcription, permissions, retention and purpose must be approved, for a local installation too.

props.title: Redact before pasting
props.scenario: Before pasting a meeting record or customer email, inspect each piece of information: Is it necessary for the purpose, covered by the approved workflow, or should it be removed? Complete two rounds; the second contains less obvious risks.
